response.answer: To operationalize agential realism, define measurable units like grant criteria and lab routines, then link them to observable indicators such as funding outcomes and research outputs. Focus on relational dynamics and material-discursive practices.

results.title: Agential Realism (Concepts & Beliefs)
results.content:
Title: Agential Realism (Concepts & Beliefs)
**Agential realism** is a **philosophical concept** that explores the ways in which **human agency** and the material world co-constitute each other. * **Agential realism** explores the intertwining of **human agency** and the material world. The concept of Agential Realism is a philosophical framework that challenges the notion of an objective **reality** existing independently of human perception and interpretation. Agential Realism was coined by **Karen Barad**, a feminist theorist who bridged the gap between the natural sciences and the humanities by intertwining quantum physics concepts with feminist epistemology. By integrating insights from diverse disciplines, Barad’s work on Agential Realism offers a nuanced understanding of the complex relationships between **ontology**, **subjectivity**, **agency**, and **social construction**. Agential realism has become a captivating concept in the realm of **literature**, offering authors a unique perspective to delve into the complexities of **human agency** and the interplay between **subjectivity** and **objectivity**. By exploring the complexities of human agency, the interplay between subjectivity and **objectivity**, and the philosophical concepts underlying agential realism, literature becomes a vehicle through which readers can gain a deeper understanding of the human condition and our place in the world. In contrast to traditional notions of agency solely attributed to humans, Agential Realism highlights the significance of **materiality** and the non-human world in shaping human agency. These characteristics of Agential Realism theory contribute to a comprehensive framework that embraces the complexities of **ontology**, subjectivity, agency, **social construction**, **relationality**, **materiality**, and **reflexivity**. Agential Realism, a philosophical perspective that focuses on the interconnectedness between human agency and larger social structures, challenges conventional dualisms and fixed meanings. By recognizing the role of human agency in shaping reality, Agential Realism urges individuals to reflect on their actions and assume **responsibility** for creating more equitable and just social realities. Agential Realism is a philosophical concept that explores the interconnectedness between human agency and the material world. Agential Realism emphasizes the situated and embodied nature of human agency, the role of materiality and the non-human world in shaping agency, and the importance of reflexivity and self-reflection in understanding human agency. Agential Realism offers a new understanding of reality that highlights the interconnectedness between human agency and social structures.

results.title: Agential realism - Wikipedia
results.content: Much of Barad's scholarly work has revolved around their concept of "agential realism," and their theories hold importance for many academic fields, including science studies, STS (Science, Technology, and Society), feminist technoscience, philosophy and philosophy of science, feminist theory, and physics. This claim is based on the fact that Barad's agential realism is a way of understanding the politics, ethics, and agencies of any act of observation, and indeed any kind of knowledge practice. For this reason, according to Barad, agential realism is useful for any kind of feminist analysis, even if the connection to science is not apparent. Karen Barad's agential realism collapses ontology and epistemology into an undifferentiated field of "intra-action," where entities and meanings continually emerge through temporary "cuts." While this framework aspires to decenter human exceptionalism, it ultimately reproduces the very anthropocentrism it seeks to escape by projecting a human concept of agency—rooted in Enlightenment individualism—onto all matter.

results.title: Agential Realism – New Materialism
results.content: Danish School of Education Research Research themes **Agential Realism – New Materialism**. In post-human and new materialist thinking, matter is instead regarded as always already entangled with discourse in the enactment of phenomena; a point that Karen Barad and agential realism emphasizes with the conceptualization of onto-epistemology. This reconfiguration occurs via conceptualizations of assemblages, for example as in Actor Network Theory and in Deleuze and Guattari’s work together, but also in the most recent developments by Karen Barad, agential realism, where the intra-activity and entangling agencies in and through material-discursive apparatuses point to such comprehensive open-ended processes as the fundamental condition of the enactment of all kinds of phenomena. At the Danish School of Education you will find agential realism discussed and applied in analyses of qualitative data in work on schools, and on architecture and gender (Malou Juelskjær); on children, young people and computer games, and on children and bullying in schools (Dorte Marie Søndergaard); and on schools and learning (Helle Plauborg).
